text: The binding of testosterone to cell receptors can rapidly (within seconds) trigger second messengers involved in downstream protein kinase signaling (49), suggesting a link between momentary post-workout elevations and muscle protein synthesis. Kvorning and colleagues (1 17) demonstrated that suppressing testosterone levels with goserelin blunted exercise-induced muscle growth despite no alterations in acute mRNA expression of MyoD, myogenin, myostatin, IGF-1Ea, IGF-1Eb, IGF1Ec, and androgen receptor, suggesting that testosterone may mediate intracellular signaling downstream from these factors.
